tasks.short: Maintain attendance, grades and required records

steps.what: Establish actual student attendance and required course-status facts from the session and available course evidence.
outputs: Observed attendance and verified status facts

steps.what: Write the actual student attendance and other required course-status records in the {LMS} draft.
Check the completed attendance and status draft against actual observations, student identity and course session.
outputs: Checked exact attendance and status version

steps.what: Commit the checked attendance and required status records in the {LMS}.
outputs: Saved actual attendance and status records

steps.what: Assemble the examiner's actual final grades and approved corrections from the {LMS}, checking course, assessment attempt and student identity before transfer.
outputs: Qualified source grade batch with unresolved exceptions

steps.what: Re-enter the qualified final grades and assessment identifiers into the student registry draft {OTHER} for the required second record.
inputs: Qualified source grade batch from s5
outputs: Staged registry grade draft, not yet committed

steps.what: Reconcile the completed registry grade draft to the final source grades, checking every student, attempt, result and exceptional correction.
outputs: Checked exact registry batch or held exceptions

steps.what: Commit only the exact reconciled grade batch in the student registry {OTHER}.
inputs: Exact registry batch checked in s7
outputs: Registered final grades with native audit record

tasks.design: Test the native {LMS}-to-student-registry {OTHER} mapping and staged import first. Replace actual grade re-entry with a deterministic draft transfer; retain attendance capture, source qualification, full batch reconciliation and the final register action. No model sets a grade.
tasks.previous_blocker: Final grades must exist in two systems with different assessment identifiers.
tasks.enabler_now: Native staged imports can map stable student, course, attempt and result fields.
tasks.still_hard: Wrong attempt, changed grades and exceptional student cases.
tasks.human_edge: Verifying that the record reflects the examiner's actual decision.

ambition.what: Remove repeated grade entry while maintaining required records.

tasks.altitude: Record responsibility stays with the teacher; grade authority is unchanged.

evidence.claim: Deterministic staged transfers can replace repeated grade entry when two required systems use stable identifiers.

assumptions: Conditional E1 active-work allocation for real required double entry, consistent with the digest's described workflow; no claim that this institution was measured. Already integrated registers give zero saving.

The examiner produces final grades in the earlier marking workflow, with no marking saving here. s5 explicitly qualifies existing student ID, course, assessment, attempt, result, scale and correction version. Missing or mismatched fields go to manual resolution; no inferred grades or free clean feed.

s6's future native transfer prepares a staged draft only. s7 checks the completed output before s8 commits. If the native system cannot stage and reconcile, retain manual entry until a safe staging method exists.
s1 produces actual attendance; s2 captures it. No attendance inference from logins or the calendar. Existing status corrections are retained, not invented as extra admin.
s3 and s7 are ordinary completed-record checks, supplying exact-version gates without new self-approval labour. Both commits retain 1% and no runtime saving. Changed records invalidate approval.
research_questions: Can the native import preserve assessment attempts, grade changes and held exceptions in a historical batch?

already_counted.description: Actual attendance capture, source qualification, all reconciliation and both commit actions remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain field mappings and resolve new import-format exceptions.

approvals.approved_version: Exact attendance and status version checked in s3
Exact completed registry grade batch reconciled in s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 25 points of actual repeated grade entry removed; less 2 mapping upkeep. No saving on observation, marking, source qualification, reconciliation or same-system commits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Supervise student teaching, internship and research

steps.what: Find and inspect the student's actual teaching, internship or research submission and prior supervision actions in the {LMS} and {DOCS}.
outputs: Relevant work and context with missing items identified

steps.what: Supervise undergraduate or graduate teaching, internship and research work through actual observation, discussion and academic feedback.
outputs: Actual feedback and agreed supervision actions

steps.what: Write and check the actual feedback and agreed actions in the supervision record {LMS}.
Save the checked supervision record privately in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure native submission filters and linked prior supervision records. Reduce finding the correct work, retaining substantive reading, direct supervision and actual feedback writing. No automated assessment or completion decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Work and prior actions are repeatedly located in separate course folders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native student and activity filters can retain the lookup context.
tasks.still_hard: Assessing research quality and responding to individual difficulties.

evidence.claim: Native submission views can reduce repeated retrieval while substantive supervision remains human.

assumptions: E1 planning allocation, not measured. Students produce actual submissions; missing work is obtained manually, not assumed present. Only repeated finding within s1 is reduced, not substantive review.
s3 actually records the outcome after supervision. s4 is a private record save, not a hidden feedback publication. Any later send needs a separate final-version gate and has no saving here.

The ordinary s3 completed-record check supplies the requested save gate without added self-approval; save effort stays at 100%. Formal grades and attendance are separately maintained in task 6082 with no double credit.
research_questions: Do filters shorten real preparation while preserving the full student work?

already_counted.description: Source inspection, supervision, actual feedback writing/checking and save remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain submission links and access after course rollover.

approvals.approved_version: Exact actual supervision record checked in s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 20 x 35% retrieval reduction = 7 gross points less 1 upkeep. Already linked submissions yield zero.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Prepare the actual regularly scheduled office-hour availability in {CALENDAR} against teaching commitments.
Write the office-hours notice for students in the {LMS}, using the actual proposed times and access details.
Check the completed calendar series and student notice against actual availability, access and intended course audience.
Save the exact checked office-hour calendar series in {CALENDAR}.
Publish the exact checked office-hours notice to the verified course audience in the {LMS}.
inputs: Exact notice and audience checked in s3

steps.what: Maintain regularly scheduled office hours to advise and assist students through actual individual conversations.
Write and check any actual necessary private follow-up note from the office-hour conversation in {DOCS}.
Save the checked necessary follow-up note in the authorised private folder {DOCS}.

tasks.design: Use native recurring availability in {CALENDAR} and reusable fixed office-hours fields in the {LMS}. They reduce repeated scheduling and notice entry only. Keep all real office-hour assistance and actual follow-up writing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stable office-hour times are manually recreated and recopied.
tasks.enabler_now: Native recurring series and reusable notice fields.

evidence.claim: Native recurring availability and fixed notice fields can reduce repeated setup, not the office-hour conversations.

assumptions: Conditional E1 allocation amortised over the office-hour cycle, not setup charged to every student. Existing recurrence and notices yield zero; no invented scheduling baseline.

The teacher produces actual slots from commitments in s1 and writes the real notice in s2. No automatic inferred availability or attendance. Private notes exist only where actually necessary and are fully retained.

s3 checks both completed artefacts and supplies separate exact-version save and publish gates. s7 supplies the private-note gate after the real conversation; no added self-approval time. Each action retains 1%.
This office-hour path covers routine assistance, not the separately counted extended curriculum/career session in task 6085; do not add duplicate student conversation time.
research_questions: Is stable availability currently recreated manually?

already_counted.description: Residual setup, final checks, office-hour assistance, actual notes and all actions remain counted.

incremental.description: Check recurring availability and notice defaults after timetable changes.

approvals.approved_version: Exact office-hour series checked in s3
Exact completed notice and audience checked in s3
Exact actual follow-up note checked in s7

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 5 x 40% plus 3 x 30% = 2.9 gross setup points less 0.5 upkeep = 2.4; high rounded down to 2. No conversation or action-tail saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find the actual current academic and vocational curricula, programme requirements and career-service information in {DOCS}.
inputs: Current approved programme and career information
outputs: Relevant source pages and unanswered questions

steps.what: Elicit the student's actual interests, circumstances and academic or career concerns in conversation.
Advise students on academic and vocational curricula and on career issues, discussing fit, trade-offs and appropriate specialist referral with the actual student.
outputs: Actual advice and agreed next steps

steps.what: Write the actual advice and source links in the follow-up note {DOCS}, checking the completed note and student recipient against the conversation.
outputs: Checked final advice note and recipient

steps.what: Save the exact checked advice note in the authorised folder {DOCS}.
Send the exact checked follow-up note to the verified student through {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: Configure source-library filters for current sociology curricula and career-service information in {DOCS}. Reduce finding relevant pages, keeping actual student discovery, personal advice and follow-up writing. No automated eligibility or career-fit decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current requirements and service pages are repeatedly found among old versions.
tasks.enabler_now: Native current-version filters and programme tags.
tasks.still_hard: Understanding individual circumstances and meaningful options.

ambition.what: Support current curriculum and career advice.

tasks.altitude: The teacher remains an adviser, not an automated eligibility authority.

evidence.claim: Current-version source filters can reduce repeated programme-information retrieval while individual advice remains human.

assumptions: E1 unmeasured allocation for a separate extended advice episode, not a second count of office-hour assistance. Existing effective source navigation gives zero.

Programme and careers staff produce the approved source pages. s1 inspects them; missing or unclear requirements are resolved manually rather than inferred. Student goals are actually elicited in s2, and s4 actually records the advice.

The normal completed-note and recipient check in s4 supplies exact save and send gates without added self-approval time. Both actions are fully retained. No enrolment, qualification, job application or referral transaction is hidden in the conversation.
research_questions: Do current-version filters reliably exclude obsolete programme requirements?

already_counted.description: Source inspection, all individual dialogue and advice, follow-up writing/checks, save and send remain counted.

incremental.description: Maintain current-source tags and remove obsolete links.

approvals.approved_version: Exact completed advice note checked in s4
Exact advice note and student recipient checked in s4

time_saved_range_pct.basis: 20 x 35% source retrieval reduction = 7 gross points less 1 upkeep. No advice, prose or transaction-tail saving.

role.altitude: Sociology teaching, student judgment and personal advice stay human.
role.ambitious_version: A teacher who removes repeated record entry and source searches while retaining academic judgment and direct student support.
